feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED. All five declared propositions are covered exactly once with matching names, single-expression bodies, and only allowed builtins (max, any, range); no forbidden calls, assignments, imports, or sibling-predicate use. key_found follows the documented view scan (image channel 0 == 5, which already excludes wall/closed-door-hidden cells) and implements the latch via env.episode_memory[previous_valuation] with a truthiness guard, so it can be true at the first step when the key is in view at reset. target_door_open and has_matching_key identify the locked door by place exactly as documented: column env.width - env.room_size over the ball's room row span range((room_size-1)*b, (room_size-1)*b + room_size), which is precisely the room's wall rows (corners are walls and are filtered by the type check); no other hallway or side-room door lies on that column, so toggling unrelated doors cannot trigger it, and the color match ties the carried key to the locked door's color even when other doors share that color. has_matching_key and target_door_open read only current state, so they correctly turn false again when the key is dropped or the door is toggled shut. target_room_entered checks the whole target room block (x >= width - room_size, agent y within the ball's room span) including the doorway column, plus the previous-valuation latch. target_picked_up matches the carried ball against env.mission rather than a hard-coded color. All grid scans guard None before attribute reads, env.carrying is guarded, the max(..., default=agent_pos[1]) fallback only matters on the terminating pickup step where it is harmless, and no predicate depends on RM state, descriptions, or rewards. The predicates reproduce the example trace transitions (hallway-door toggle at step 6 leaves target_door_open false; doorway standing at step 33 sets target_room_entered) and satisfy the declared ordering constraints.
